title: EDA — TV, Radio, Newspaper vs Sales
description: Run a first real EDA: correlations, plots, quartile bins, and a findings memo.
overview_content:
Lab intro

First Real EDA Track: Correlation, Plots, Findings Memo

Scenario: Marketing asks which channel drives Sales. Load Advertising.csv (200 rows), compute correlations, plot scatters, bin TV into quartiles, and write a 5-bullet findings memo. You will learn: pandas read_csv / describe / corr, matplotlib scatter, correlation vs causation. Time: ~45 minutes. Level: Beginner. Needs: pandas + matplotlib. Env: 🟢 Colab only.
steps_content:
Exercises (do these!)

Exercise 1 — Full correlation matrix

Print df[["TV","Radio","Newspaper","Sales"]].corr() rounded to 4 d.p. Which pair of features (not Sales) is most correlated? Expected: Radio–Newspaper ≈ 0.3541 is the strongest feature–feature pair (TV pairs are ≈ 0.05).

Follow-up: What fraction of Sales variance does TV alone explain (R squared)? Check: about 0.6118.

Hint 
c = df[["TV", "Radio", "Newspaper"]].corr()
print(c)
# upper triangle only to avoid duplicates

Exercise 2 — Highest single-feature R vs Sales

Using absolute correlation with Sales, which feature wins and what is r? Expected: TV, r ≈ 0.7822.

Follow-up: How large is the Q4 minus Q1 mean-sales lift? Check: 10.076.

Hint

df.corr()["Sales"].drop("Sales").abs().idxmax() / .max().

Exercise 3 — TV quartiles → mean Sales

Bin TV into 4 equal-count bins (pd.qcut(..., 4)), print mean Sales per bin. Expected: Q1 8.39 · Q2 12.686 · Q3 16.548 · Q4 18.466 (50 rows each).

Follow-up: How much variance do Radio and Newspaper share (r squared)? Check: about 0.1254.

Hint

pd.qcut(df["TV"], 4, labels=["Q1","Q2","Q3","Q4"]) then groupby(...).mean().
